message.content:
# The Last Day of Summer

The last day of summer hangs in amber light,
a borrowed hour stretched thin with gold.
The heat still clings like a memory refusing to leave,
yet the air has turned—cooler now, aware of its own departure.

Somewhere a child runs through a sprinkler one final time,
laughing at the cold shock, not knowing
this is the last time the garden will smell
of cut grass and roses left to wither.

The beach chairs fold like tired wings,
the sandcastle's ghost already dissolving.
We pretend we knew this was coming,
that we were ready, that we planned
to leave the sun-soaked hours behind.

But no one is ready.
The peaches are too ripe now,
the crickets too loud in their last chorus.
The shadows grow longer, reaching for us
like a hand that cannot quite hold on.

And when evening comes, we stand at the door
of the house we will not see until next year,
and the last bee hums a note of pure gold—
then silence. Then autumn. Then the long forgetting.
